decisions.quote:
Specifically, we revisited Loftus et al.’s (1978) study, focusing on
the 1-day delayed questionnaire condition of Experiment 3, to
provide a contemporary validation of the misinformation effect.
When implementing a GTA-based video of the car-pedestrian
collision and videotaped cowitness narrative in an online setting, we
successfully replicated the original misinformation effect. Misled
participants were more likely to report the incorrect traffic sign
information compared with control participants (i.e., 34% difference
in accuracy between conditions), yielding a moderate effect (Cramer’s
V = 0.37).
decisions.parent_source_context: Parent read original-specific design, all three new studies and GeneralDiscussion. Authors expressly report successfully replicating Loftus/Miller/Burns1978Experiment3one-day postevent misinformation effect with the GTA accident/cowitness paradigm. Study2betting/incentive test also shows the effect; Study3reverses event/misinformation order to investigate mechanism and compares other reversed-order originals. Its variation is not an original postevent-effect failure. The explicit overall source statement supports successful, rather than transferring a new mechanism contrast to mixed.

decisions.quote:
The purpose of our study was to replicate and extend Wolfe et al. (2018) by examining agreement between visual inspection and the conservative dual-criteria method. We extended Wolfe et al. by using a larger number of graphs to examine within-subject error, blinded normalized graphs, and modified reversal/withdrawal designs.
A secondary purpose was to replicate and extend Lanovaz and Hranchuk (2021) by examining correspondence between visual inspection, the conservative dual-criteria method, and the machine-learning algorithms on a novel dataset. We extended both studies by using clinical data and adding a 10-point scale with definitional criteria to visual-inspection ratings.
decisions.parent_source_context: Parent inspected primary original-findings description, Methods, new clinical graph construction, new independent ratings and stated replication aims. Wolfe2018agreement was measured on31published multiple-baseline graphs; current authors test correspondence again using198newclinical AB comparisons from6participants and5newdoctoral raters. New data and new judgments directly retest the published empirical agreement finding; applying an algorithm does not turn this into a reproduction on the original graph/rating dataset. Both shipped and blind replication type agree and are source-supported. No unrequested outcome judgment is added.

decisions.quote:
Eriksson and Coultas (2009) found no
     conformity bias using quizzes in which the answers were not objectively fixed as correct or incorrect (e.g., belief,
     preference, and norm). We replicated their experiment using questions with fixed answers. In this study (N = 120),
     after participants answered “yes/no” to 14 questions, they were informed of the four patterns of the distribution of
     the other nine participants’ responses (9, 6, 3, 0 participants said “yes”). Then, participants completed the same
     questions again. The results showed that conformity bias was observed. We discuss the inconsistency of the results
     between the previous study and our study.
decisions.parent_source_context: Parent read complete English abstract and Japanese original-specific Methods/Results/Discussion. CurrentN120new-data experiment finds majority conformity in objective AND attitude items; the latter preserves the prior question class. The section explicitly headed inconsistency with previous research says its results are inconsistent with Eriksson/Coultas2009inverse-S/nonconformist pattern, considering both question-type and within-versus-between-participant design explanations. This is authors stated original-specific failure, not failure inferred solely from a new objective-item extension or new p-values. Design limitations call for further tests but do not declare the current evidence uninformative. Shipped failed is supported.
